caption:
An alert that can't survive cross-examination is worse than no alert at all.

We build the collection plan around three states: confirmed, assessed, unknown. Confirmed means evidence traced to a timestamp. Assessed means a judgment call, labeled as one. Unknown means we say so and stop there. Nothing gets rounded up to sound more finished than it is.

That discipline exists because these products end up in front of a magistrate, a board of inquiry, or a commander who has to justify a decision. If a claim can't hold up under questioning, it doesn't belong in the brief. Evidence over assertion is not a slogan here — it's the only thing that keeps the output usable when someone challenges it.

Evidence over assertion. Named limits over silent gaps. That's the operating rule, not a mission statement.
